title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued its reply to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its approach to making AI safer, more transparent and accountable. It highlights key actions, such as strengthening regulation, boosting research, and encouraging collaboration between industry, academia and regulators to uphold high public standards for AI.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, focusing on maintaining fairness, accuracy, and trust in assessment processes. This approach was developed following requests from the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted material and evaluates the legal, economic, and ethical effects of that practice. It identifies potential risks and offers guidelines and policy recommendations to protect creators while encouraging responsible AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has released a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, outlining its approach to tackling the challenges and opportunities presented by artificial intelligence in the UK. It stresses the need for decisive action, details policy measures to promote responsible AI development, strengthen regulation, and support the growth of the UK’s AI industry.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document explains the role and responsibilities of the committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence affects public standards. It also answers common questions about the review process and how decisions will be made.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. In the submission, they outline their views on how AI should be regulated and managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how AI technologies will reshape the rules and procedures for approving and monitoring medical products, ensuring they remain safe and effective. It outlines practical ways to embed the principles from the AI White Paper into existing regulatory frameworks.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI entity worldwide for its size. It focuses on building a strong AI capability to support operations and maintain strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the UK’s Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness AI’s benefits while addressing its risks. It establishes frameworks for safe, innovative AI adoption across transport services, balancing opportunity with risk management.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyright‑protected content has been used to train and improve AI systems, assessing compliance with legal provisions. It outlines progress, challenges, and recommendations for aligning AI development with copyright law under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
